topic: Changes in Solid Materials When Hammered or Cut
key_concepts: Solid materials can be hammered or cut
Hammering can change a solid's size and shape
Cutting can change a solid's size and shape
Hammering or cutting does not form a new material
Only physical appearance changes when solids are hammered or cut
Malleable materials can be hammered into shapes or thin sheets
Gold and silver are malleable and used in jewelry
Ductile materials can be stretched into wires without breaking
Gold, silver, and copper are ductile
Brittle materials such as crayons, pencils, and twigs break easily
Metals are often shiny and conduct heat and electricity
Not all solids can be cut with ordinary scissors; iron and steel need special cutters
